newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: SERBIA ADOPTS LONG-TERM FARM STRATEGY - PAPER.
newsitem.headline: SERBIA ADOPTS LONG-TERM FARM STRATEGY - PAPER.

text.p: Serbia has for the first time adopted a long-term strategy for the development of villages, agriculture, food industry, forestry and water resources management, the Belgrade daily Borba reported on Monday.

Priority has been given to livestock breeding, the cultivation of fruit, vegetables, grapes and industrial crops (sugar beet, sunflower, soybean and hops), raising the grains yield, seed production, aromatic and medicinal herbs, healthy food and the food industry, Serbian Agriculture Minister Jovan Babovic was quoted by the paper as saying.
The government had also set aside 75 million German marks for buying up this year's wheat crop, estimated at over 3.1 million tonnes.
It had earmarked 54 million marks for the development of cattle-breeding and 40 million marks for picking, buying up and exporting early fruits.
The funds for livestock development would be used for the purchase of 10,000 heifers, 10,000 bull calves and 40,000 sows. Ten million marks would be spent on poultry production, Babovic said.
According to the long-term strategy, earnings from exports of agricultural products would exceed an annual $2 billion by the year 2000, Babovic said.
"Already by the year 2010 exports would exceed $5 million and by 2020 double to $10 million dollars per year," he added.
The government's primary goal was to revive village farms.

Individual producers would be able to get credits through slaughterhouses, dairies, farm cooperatives and socially-owned agricultural firms which would conclude agreements with the Serbian Commodity Reserve Agency, Babovic said.
The government had also earmarked funds for various programmes to revive agricultural production.
"Programmes 1 and 2 for the revival of agricultural machinery are of vast importance for the development of agriculture," Babovic said.
A total of 205 million dinars ($33.19 million) was invested in the first part of the scheme which has produced excellent results.
"But the needs for machinery were much greater and the government has therefore decided to set aside another 100 million German marks for Programme 2," he added.

In the second stage, 29 machine producers and 100 sub-contractors were obliged to deliver more than 4,000 tractors, 270 combines, 280 maize harvesters and other auxiliary farm equipment to the Serbian Commodity Reserve Agency which would exchange them for agricultural produce.

The strategy set out a long-term agrarian policy, an agrarian budget and a new land policy aimed at increasing the area of individual farms by joining smaller properties through economic and inheritance policy, the report said, but did not specify.
